chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Abdullah who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about voluntary prayer on Friday, so he said: 'Six rak'at in the early part of the day, and six rak'at before midday, and two rak'at when midday passes, and six rak'at after the Friday prayer; that is twenty rak'at besides the obligatory prayer.'

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: Midday (when the sun begins to decline)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed number and timing of voluntary prayers on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) details a structured regimen of twenty voluntary rak'at on Friday, emphasizing the day's spiritual merit through specific timings such as before and after midday (zawal). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the significance of Friday as a weekly Eid, where consistent nafl prayers serve to purify the soul and prepare the believer for the congregational Dhuhr prayer. The distribution reflects a holistic approach to worship, integrating devotion throughout the day rather than concentrating it solely in one segment.
